why: We fund a handful of companies a year, so we need two things on day one: users who can't live without it and one founder we'd follow anywhere. Here a third of the first families left in two months, and you couldn't tell us who leads.
fix: Show that people love it: get the families still paying to stay month after month, and bring back what the 19 who left told you and what the 41 who stayed would do if Tidy shut off.
Name one lead founder and tell the story of something hard they kept pushing through, so we can see why we'd follow that person for ten years.
Bring proof of love that you didn't pay for: families telling friends, the waitlist growing beyond the one newsletter post, people asking for more.

quotes.note: 19 of your first 60 families left in about two months. Loved products don't lose a third of their first users that fast.

quotes.words: What the 19 who left said, and what the 41 would do without Tidy: [not answered]
quotes.note: We asked what users would do without you and got no answer. That was the love test, and it went blank.

quotes.words: Which one is the lead: [not answered]
quotes.note: We back one founder. With no lead named, we have no one to bet on.

quotes.words: The waitlist of 400 came from one parenting newsletter post.
quotes.note: Good early interest, but it is one post, not users bringing in other users.
